questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black text or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to stay in control of a motorcycle during a turn?

options.text: Accelerate through the turn.
Reduce your speed before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate through the turn.
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, slow down before entering it. Look where you want to go. Press on the handlebar to lean the right way. Then gently add throttle as you go through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: If a motorcyclist cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should they do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat protects you from impact.
Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle and must ride over it, slow down first. Then approach it at a 90-degree angle if you can.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic?

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra careful when entering an intersection.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, who goes first?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake gives the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes together every time you stop.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous for a motorcyclist to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can see you more easily.
You may not see road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. That vehicle could swerve into your lane and hit you. It could also block your way to escape if danger appears ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go less than 25 mph. Examples include farm tractors, construction equipment, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated if their blood alcohol content (BAC) is ____ or higher.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or more means you are intoxicated. You cannot legally operate a motor vehicle if you are intoxicated.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.question: If you have a passenger on your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Leave more distance to stop.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which changes how the motorcycle handles. Ride slower and allow more stopping distance. The passenger should grip the passenger handgrips or hold onto your waist, hips, or midsection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will merge.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to watch the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up in work zones. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down and shift down, then quickly speed up as the dog gets close.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and shift down, then quickly speed up as the dog gets close.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches, slow down and downshift until you get close to it. Then quickly speed up and pull away from the dog.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not encouraged because you can never get used to any part of the lane.
Discouraged because it confuses other drivers.
Smart when adapting to changing road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Smart when adapting to changing road conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for all motorcycle operators.
Required for operators who have held their license for less than two years.
Required for operators under age 21.
Never required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for operators under age 21.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, all riders under age 21 must wear helmets and eye protection. Helmets and eye protection are strongly recommended for all riders.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: A trailer adds weight, so the motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the sign or signal, then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move into the part of the lane where other drivers can see you earliest.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn only your shoulders, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Eye protection is:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Recommended, not required.
Only required for new riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Wherever you are most comfortable.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling into traffic. Stay alert and adjust your position as needed.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately. Then apply it again with controlled pressure.

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: On the footrests for balance.
Pointing downward with your toes.
Relaxed and loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they could get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcycle rider should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, slow down and choose a lane position that makes you visible. Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce your reaction time. Do not speed up or make sudden changes, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
A traffic signal is ahead.
Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked to stop faster.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure immediately. Then re-apply it with gentle, controlled pressure.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders together to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead through the turn. Turn only your head and keep your eyes level with the horizon. Do not turn your shoulders, as this may cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycle brakes?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Both brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Slow down while in the turn.
Turn by using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before entering the turn, not during it.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: Not until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you think you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
